title: Free Deep Learning & Computer Vision Foundations from Stanford
post_text:
How Convolutional Neural Networks actually process image tensors:

1. Convolution Layer:
Applies kernel filters across the spatial input volume to extract local feature maps (edges, textures, shapes).

2. Activation (ReLU / GELU):
Introduces non-linearity, allowing the network to compute complex boundary mappings without vanishing gradients.

3. Pooling (Max / Average):
Reduces spatial resolution while preserving dominant feature activations, providing translational invariance.

4. Fully Connected Layers & Softmax:
Flattens high-dimensional feature activations into class probability distributions.

title: Transformer Architecture & Self-Attention Mathematical Breakdown
post_text:
The landmark 2017 paper 'Attention Is All You Need' replaced recurrent networks with pure Multi-Head Attention mechanisms.

Core Building Blocks:
1. Scaled Dot-Product Attention:
Attention(Q, K, V) = softmax(Q K^T / sqrt(d_k)) V

2. Multi-Head Projection:
Allows the model to jointly attend to information from different representation subspaces at different positions.

3. Positional Encodings:
Since there is no recurrence or convolution, sinusoidal positional encodings inject relative token order.

Attached is the original landmark research paper from Google Brain.

title: Fine-Tuning LLMs with LoRA & Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT)
post_text:
Full parameter fine-tuning of 70B+ LLMs requires massive GPU clusters. LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) freezes pre-trained weights and injects trainable rank decomposition matrices.

Why LoRA is Revolutionary:
1. Reduces trainable parameters by 10,000x and GPU memory footprint by 3x.
2. Injects low-rank decomposition matrices W0 + B*A into Transformer attention layers.
3. Zero inference latency overhead: trained adapter weights can be merged directly into base weights during deployment.

Attached is the original LoRA research paper by Edward Hu et al. from Microsoft.

title: 4-Bit Quantization & Memory Optimization with QLoRA
post_text:
How QLoRA enables fine-tuning 65B parameter models on a single 48GB GPU without performance degradation:

Information-theoretically optimal quantile quantization for normally distributed weights.

Quantizes the quantization constants, saving an average of 0.37 bits per parameter.

3. Paged Optimizers:
Uses NVIDIA unified memory to manage gradient checkpoint memory spikes and prevent out-of-memory errors during long sequence training.

title: Deep Residual Learning: ResNet Architecture & Skip Connections
post_text:
Why deep neural networks degraded during training before 2015 and how ResNet solved the vanishing gradient problem:

1. The Degradation Problem:
As network depth increased, accuracy saturated and degraded rapidly due to optimization difficulties.

2. Identity Shortcut Mapping:
Instead of fitting an underlying mapping H(x), residual blocks explicitly fit a residual mapping F(x) = H(x) - x, giving H(x) = F(x) + x.

3. Gradient Highway:
Gradients flow directly through identity shortcuts without diminishing across 100+ layers during backpropagation.

Attached is the original landmark paper by Kaiming He et al. from Microsoft Research.

title: Stanford CS230: Recurrent Neural Networks & Sequence Modeling
post_text:
Understanding Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN), LSTM, and GRU sequence architectures:

1. Standard RNN:
Computes hidden state activations sequentially: h_t = tanh(W_hh * h_{t-1} + W_xh * x_t + b_h). Suffers from vanishing / exploding gradients.

2. LSTM (Long Short-Term Memory):
Controls memory flow via 3 gates: Forget Gate (f_t), Input Gate (i_t), and Output Gate (o_t) with dedicated cell state (C_t).

3. GRU (Gated Recurrent Unit):
Simplifies LSTM by combining cell state and hidden state, using Reset (r_t) and Update (z_t) gates.

Attached is the official Stanford CS230 RNN and Sequence Modeling cheatsheet.
